title: The Pattern Matters, Not the Amount

scenes.tts: A female rhesus monkey can no longer drive her pituitary from her hypothalamus. Researchers give her the missing hormone, G n R H, through a drip. Given steadily, it fails. Given as a short burst once an hour, it works. Why would timing matter more than amount?
scenes.caption: A female rhesus monkey can no longer drive her pituitary from her hypothalamus. Researchers give her the missing hormone, GnRH, through a drip. Given steadily, it fails. Given as a short burst once an hour, it works. Why would timing matter more than amount?
scenes.visual: A drip of the hormone into the pituitary: a steady band is crossed out, hourly bursts are ticked, and timing and amount sit either side of a question mark.
scenes.narration: A female rhesus monkey can no longer drive her pituitary from her hypothalamus. Researchers give her the missing hormone, GnRH, through a drip. Given steadily, it fails. Given as a short burst once an hour, it works. Why would timing matter more than amount?

scenes.tts: In mammals, neurons in the hypothalamus release G n R H into portal vessels. The vessels carry it to the anterior pituitary. There, G n R H triggers release of two hormones, L H and F S H. These gonadotropins act on the gonads. G n R H is released in pulses. Together, the three organs form the hypothalamic pituitary gonadal axis.
scenes.caption: In mammals, neurons in the hypothalamus release GnRH into portal vessels. The vessels carry it to the anterior pituitary. There, GnRH triggers release of two hormones, LH and FSH. These gonadotropins act on the gonads. GnRH is released in pulses. Together, the three organs form the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis.
scenes.visual: Three labelled blocks in a row, hypothalamus, anterior pituitary, gonads, joined by arrows for GnRH in portal vessels and for LH and FSH.
scenes.narration: In mammals, neurons in the hypothalamus release GnRH into portal vessels. The vessels carry it to the anterior pituitary. There, GnRH triggers release of two hormones, LH and FSH. These gonadotropins act on the gonads. GnRH is released in pulses. Together, the three organs form the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis.

scenes.tts: In 1978, Belchetz, Plant, Nakai, Keogh and Knobil studied female rhesus monkeys, asking whether the pulses matter. Lesions of the hypothalamus had abolished L H and F S H secretion. The pituitary was intact. So the team could replace G n R H by intravenous infusion, either continuously or as brief infusions once an hour, and read the pituitary's answer in blood samples.
scenes.caption: In 1978, Belchetz, Plant, Nakai, Keogh and Knobil studied female rhesus monkeys, asking whether the pulses matter. Lesions of the hypothalamus had abolished LH and FSH secretion. The pituitary was intact. So the team could replace GnRH by intravenous infusion, either continuously or as brief infusions once an hour, and read the pituitary's answer in blood samples.
scenes.visual: The axis redrawn for the monkey: the hypothalamus block is crossed by a lesion and its link to the pituitary is cut, the pituitary is marked intact, and a drip line feeds GnRH into it.
scenes.narration: In 1978, Belchetz, Plant, Nakai, Keogh and Knobil studied female rhesus monkeys, asking whether the pulses matter. Lesions of the hypothalamus had abolished LH and FSH secretion. The pituitary was intact. So the team could replace GnRH by intravenous infusion, either continuously or as brief infusions once an hour, and read the pituitary's answer in blood samples.

scenes.tts: First, a continuous infusion. The pituitary has the hormone all the time. If it read only the total amount, the steady drip should have worked at least as well as pulses. It did not. Continuous infusion failed to sustain L H and F S H secretion.
scenes.caption: First, a continuous infusion. The pituitary has the hormone all the time. If it read only the total amount, the steady drip should have worked at least as well as pulses. It did not. Continuous infusion failed to sustain LH and FSH secretion.
scenes.visual: A steady yellow band grows along a time line under the rig while the LH and FSH output stays red: not sustained.
scenes.narration: First, a continuous infusion. The pituitary has the hormone all the time. If it read only the total amount, the steady drip should have worked at least as well as pulses. It did not. Continuous infusion failed to sustain LH and FSH secretion.

scenes.tts: Next, brief infusions once an hour. Hourly pulses restored L H and F S H secretion. The authors also reported that returning to the hourly schedule brought secretion back after the steady infusion.
scenes.caption: Next, brief infusions once an hour. Hourly pulses restored LH and FSH secretion. The authors also reported that returning to the hourly schedule brought secretion back after the steady infusion.
scenes.visual: Short yellow bursts, once an hour, on a second time line. The LH and FSH output turns green: restored. An arrow from the steady line to the hourly line marks the return.
scenes.narration: Next, brief infusions once an hour. Hourly pulses restored LH and FSH secretion. The authors also reported that returning to the hourly schedule brought secretion back after the steady infusion.

scenes.tts: The authors concluded that the pattern of G n R H, not its total amount, controls the pituitary. The experiment shows pattern reading in this primate. It does not show where the pulses come from, or what interval is normal in humans. In mice, switching on kisspeptin neurons in the hypothalamus evoked L H pulses. Whether they do so in primates is a separate question. A steady supply is not more G n R H. Held steady, it turns the pituitary down.
scenes.caption: The authors concluded that the pattern of GnRH, not its total amount, controls the pituitary. The experiment shows pattern reading in this primate. It does not show where the pulses come from, or what interval is normal in humans. In mice, switching on kisspeptin neurons in the hypothalamus evoked LH pulses. Whether they do so in primates is a separate question. A steady supply is not more GnRH. Held steady, it turns the pituitary down.
scenes.visual: Side by side: steady band into the pituitary, which is turned down; hourly bursts into the pituitary, which gives LH and FSH. A note says what the experiment does not show.
scenes.narration: The authors concluded that the pattern of GnRH, not its total amount, controls the pituitary. The experiment shows pattern reading in this primate. It does not show where the pulses come from, or what interval is normal in humans. In mice, switching on kisspeptin neurons in the hypothalamus evoked LH pulses. Whether they do so in primates is a separate question. A steady supply is not more GnRH. Held steady, it turns the pituitary down.
